messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away) and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (≈ 170,000 km). Its mass is estimated to be around 10–20 times that of Jupiter, making it one of the most massive “hot Jupiters” known.  

(Other very large exoplanets—such as HD 106906 b or WASP‑17b—are slightly smaller, so HD 100546 b remains the record holder.)
